meta.title: Command Palette
meta.description: A fully-engineered ⌘K command menu with fuzzy search, two-tier tab filtering, keyboard navigation, grouped results, avatar support, and a keyboard shortcut footer.

blocks.content: The ⌘K pattern is table stakes for serious products. But most implementations stop at a search input over a flat list. This one goes further: two independent tab rows, avatar rendering with graceful fallbacks, grouped results with section headers, and a footer row of keyboard shortcuts that looks designed rather than bolted on.

Fuzzy search is implemented from scratch — no Fuse.js, no external dependency. The scoring algorithm weighs contiguous character matches higher than scattered ones, so "hp" surfaces "Harper" before "Help pages". Results update on every keystroke. Sections that score zero are removed entirely, not just greyed out.

blocks.title: Two tab rows, one model
blocks.content: Source tabs filter by where data comes from (Gmail, Figma, Linear). Filter tabs filter by what it is (People, Docs, Tasks). Both are optional and independent. An item passes the filter when it matches the active source AND the active filter — or when either tab is set to "All".
Press ⌘K to open the palette. Type to search, use ↑↓ to navigate, Enter to select.
Wrap your app with CommandPaletteRoot and pass your sections. The ⌘K shortcut is wired automatically.
Items are grouped into sections. Each section has a title shown as a header above its items. Results are filtered and sorted by fuzzy score when the user types.

blocks.title: Avatar rendering
blocks.content: The icon field accepts a URL string (renders an ), a React node (renders as-is), or you can use initials + initialsColor for a coloured avatar fallback.
The palette supports two independent tab rows. Source tabs filter by integration (e.g. Gmail, Figma). Filter tabs filter by content type (People, Tasks, Files). Both are optional.

items.q: Does Command Palette require Fuse.js or cmdk?
items.a: No! Command Palette includes an in-house scoring algorithm designed specifically for instant sub-millisecond filtering with zero external npm dependencies.

items.q: Can I trigger the modal programmatically without pressing ⌘K?
items.a: Yes! Use the useCommandPalette() hook anywhere inside your component tree and call open() or toggle().
